topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, sets the lecture within the broader cancer course, and outlines the primary learning objectives.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetics, Chance, and Environmental Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the baseline origins of cancer by evaluating how endogenous mutations, random chance, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures contribute to cancer incidence globally.

topics.label: Pathogen-Induced Carcinogenesis and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, featuring a detailed case study on the geographical and molecular mechanisms underlying Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Direct Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific chemical and physical mutagens damage DNA directly or require host metabolic conversion into reactive carcinogens that form DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between tumor initiators and promoters, highlighting how chronic inflammation, signaling mimics, and developmental life stages create permissive environments for malignant growth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic signatures, epidemiological studies, animal models, and in vitro tests used to determine whether agents cause cancer, along with their associated limitations and risk considerations.
